messages:
Sam: Ran a perfetto capture on staging-dedicated yesterday to investigate a token-latency spike during batching. Initial looks point at repeated kernel reconfiguration (cudnn/matmul) and a lot of small cudaMalloc/free activity in the KV cache miss path. Trace attached (see snippets below).

Maya: Can you paste the perfetto kernel timeline snippet? Did you capture from inside the container or on the host?

Sam: Captured from inside the container but non-privileged -> perfetto daemon only showed coarse events. I re-ran with nsys in privileged job and got proper kernel names. Key snippet from the perfetto timeline:```
[PERFETTO TIMELINE]
ms   kernel_name               dur_us
10234 cuBlasGemm                 120
10258 cudaMemcpyAsync             40
10300 cudaLaunchKernel          9000  <-- big spike
10310 cudaFree                    15
10350 cudaMalloc                 200
10400 custom_kv_lookup           500
```

Alex: If you were non-privileged the profiler can't get kernel symbols / timeline details. For k8s we either run the capture as privileged or mount the nvidia-container-toolkit socket (/var/run/nvidia/). Also check /dev/nvidia* perms and the driver socket (e.g., /run/nvidia/driver.sock).

InfraBot: deploy-bot: Perf capture job perf-capture-174822 scheduled on stg-node-3 (privileged=true) :white_check_mark:

Jin: Reproduced locally. When I replaced per-request cudaMalloc/cudaFree with a pre-allocated GPU pool the 9ms cudaLaunch spike disappeared. Also saw batching heuristic flip: small batches (1-2 requests) forced an immediate flush which caused more kernel churn. nvprof excerpt:```
==PROF==  Time(%)  Time   Calls   Avg us   Min us  Max us  Name
 62.3   1.23s    120   10250    9000    12000  cudnn_convolution
 14.8   0.29s    540     540      20      800  cudaMemcpyAsync
  8.1   0.16s    860     186      10      1200  kernel_launch_dispatch
```

Maya: Good repro. So action items: 1) run privileged nsys/perfetto on next canary, 2) add quick instrumentation in KV cache to avoid per-miss allocations, 3) adjust batching thresholds so we don't flush on tiny micro-batches (tune to prefer 4-8 token groups), 4) verify node socket perms are set by our nvidia bootstrap.

Alex: I'll schedule the canary: staging canary at 1748223000 with nvidia-container-toolkit socket mount and privileged capture. I'll also add a runbook snippet in the canary job about file perms to check.

Sam: One more note — discovered the node driver socket /run/nvidia/driver.sock had 660 root:root so the capture container couldn't access symbols; chmod 666 on the host fixed it for the privileged job. Might be a packaging issue in our node bootstrap.

Jin: Also worth adding a small microbenchmark that allocates a pool vs per-request alloc/free so future regressions are caught in CI. I can PR a benchmark tomorrow.

Maya: Perfect. @Alex please add links to the perf traces and nsys output in the canary ticket when you create it. :memo: 

Alex: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
